p: A good escape game is about pacing as much as brainpower. In the first few minutes, resist the urge to start solving straight away. Search the room thoroughly, gather everything that looks useful, and lay it out where everyone can see it. Then start matching things up. Teams that do this tend to fly through the middle of the game, while those who dive straight into the first padlock can get bogged down.

It's worth thinking about who you bring, too. Four or five people often feels like the sweet spot, enough hands to search but not so many that people end up standing around. If you've got a bigger crowd, booking two rooms side by side and comparing times afterwards adds a cheeky competitive edge. Loser buys the coffees, obviously.
Colchester town centre is compact and walkable, so you can park up once and do the whole lot on foot, from the shops to the history.

Once you're out, Colchester's town centre has some real gems within walking distance. Firstsite, the contemporary art gallery with its distinctive curved golden building, is a free and family-friendly stop. The Dutch Quarter, a pretty tangle of old streets just north of the High Street, takes its name from the Flemish weavers who settled there, and it's a lovely spot for a quiet wander. Keep an eye out for Jumbo, the huge Victorian water tower that looms over the west of the centre, and for Balkerne Gate, the remains of the Roman gateway into the town. The Mercury Theatre is right nearby too if you fancy rounding off the day with a show.
